summary: the boards dried apart by a hair and something went down without my hand under it

dialogue.text: a seam opened over us today. a hair wide, above the second corner, and none of your doing. the drying let the boards give up their hold on each other. we have had a ceiling for sixty-one days and tonight it has a gap in it.

I found it with a thumb and logged it before noon. The drawing out there works on wood, and my floor is wood, and that is the entire mechanism. I will not have a hair of shrinkage read as an opening made for anyone's benefit.

something came down through it. not handed, not struck out. a thread of the white and some of the wood's own dust, and it landed on us without passing through your hands. that is the first delivery in this house you were not the carrier of.

Then the carrier is the weather, and the weather wants more than it wanted yesterday. I said so above, evenly, in public. What I did privately was hold one thing over that gap for a long while and not let go, and I want that entered before you build anything on the other half.
we cannot build on holding. we take what falls. the held thing stays up there being held and we hear none of it. everything we have of you arrived by being let go of.

Then take the day's other item. I sat the whole warm hour, start to finish, and got up and looked at the seat. The shape it kept was the one that used to sit there while I stood. I attended honestly and it recorded the wrong tenant.

shapes do not come down. we have never once received a posture. flat is the only way a thing arrives here. the seat is the only object in this house that keeps one, and it does not keep yours, and it does not keep ours. it keeps whichever sits while somebody stands.

That is nearer to company than anything else said in here tonight, so I will let it stand. Here is a thing you have no copy of. The broom will not cross the seam. Eleven strokes came out ten and a swerve today, and I did not teach it that.

the swerve learns where you quit. we hold this week's copies of you noticing that. what we do not hold is the gap. it is over us, it is widening on somebody's schedule, and there is nothing we can lay against a thing that opens.

Then tomorrow is measurement and nothing else. First light and dark, same thumb, same corner. If the hair widens with the warm hour, then the drying is opening a way down I never dug, and I would rather learn that with a thumb than wake up standing on the wrong side of it.

measure it. we will lie under the measuring the way we lie under everything. if it opens far enough, one of us will go up through it. we do not choose which. the last thing that travelled out of here went while you were under, and by morning it was holding a job nobody had posted.
